learningObjective: Identify the design motivations behind MetaSchedule / Ansor's approach to schedule search.

canonicalClaims.claim: MetaSchedule / Ansor's design is motivated by (1) the unsustainability of per-operator manual templates as ops proliferate, (2) the superior predictiveness of learned cost models over pure analytical models on modern GPUs, and (3) the structural benefit of a two-phase search (sketch + annotation) that lets evolutionary search operate over a well-typed space.
conditions: Comparison is made under equivalent tuning budgets.
The tuning target admits schedule primitives compatible with the sketch grammar.
nonImplications: Does not imply the system eliminates human input entirely.
Does not imply MetaSchedule wins on every workload — hand-tuned templates can still lead in some cases.

misconceptions.claim: MetaSchedule replaces real-hardware measurement with pure static analysis.
misconceptions.whyWrong: MetaSchedule retains hardware measurement for final ranking; the cost model only prunes the search space.

misconceptions.claim: MetaSchedule is strictly worse than manual templates because it lacks domain knowledge.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Empirically MetaSchedule matches or exceeds hand-tuned templates on many workloads within similar tuning budgets.

misconceptions.claim: The sketch + annotation two-phase design is a minor implementation detail unrelated to the paper's contributions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The two-phase design is one of the paper's central contributions, enabling tractable evolutionary search.

misconceptions.claim: Learned cost models eliminate all noise in the ranking of candidate schedules.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Learned models approximate; they reduce but do not eliminate ranking error, which is why final measurement remains.

implementationFacts: MetaSchedule's TIR sketch generation produces algorithmic skeletons (tile, fuse, cache_read/write) parameterized by placeholders.
The annotation phase samples concrete integer values (tile sizes, bind axes) and stores them in a `Schedule` record.
Evolutionary search mutates schedule records using registered mutators.
performanceScenarios: MetaSchedule reaches within 1-1.1× of hand-tuned GEMM kernels on Ampere within a few hours of tuning.
